spec_match.rationale: Reads the same path via getPathData() and getPathData({normalize:true}) and checks the spec's core normalize contract in-page: output must be absolute M/L/C/Z only, with a live verdict that can go red if a build violates it.

interactive.rationale: Three sample buttons (aria-pressed state) re-run both real readings and update two tables, two renderings, and the comparison readout.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Card promises raw-vs-normalized side by side with identical rendering; the page shows exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers relative, H/V, quadratic, smooth-shorthand and arc inputs plus the unsupported fallback, but does not yet visualize the arc-to-cubic approximation error the explainer calls out as lossy.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/4787972240179200 and the normalize spec anchor are linked.

conformance.rationale: The suite's normalize-emits-only-absolute-mlcz and preserves-relative-commands script assertions pin the same contract the page demonstrates.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153 (Playwright CDP, chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable) drove all three samples in both flag modes at both viewports: flagged runs showed raw {M C S Q T} vs normalized {M C} with matching renders; zero console errors, zero failed requests, screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the MLCZ-only contract on supported builds and the explicit fallback on unsupported ones.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, aria-pressed buttons restyle with accent-blue on ivory-text (AA), panes collapse to one column under 640px.

accessibility.rationale: Sample group has role=group with a label, buttons expose pressed state, tables have captions and scoped headers, readout is aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (two-pane grid stacks), legible tables, 44px buttons; desktop 1280x800 shows side-by-side panes as designed.

openQuestions.title: Visualize the arc-to-cubic approximation error
openQuestions.detail: The explainer notes A-to-C conversion is inherently lossy while Q-to-C is exact. A concept that overlays the original arc and its normalized cubic at exaggerated scale, measuring maximum deviation via getPointAtLength sampling on both, would turn that footnote into something observable.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use grid with explicit column collapse at narrow widths instead of letting columns squeeze.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The two comparison panes are a 1fr/1fr grid that becomes a single column under 640px; verified no overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wrap wide tables in their own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both segment tables sit in .table-wrap with overflow-x auto.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible status updates live region after button action
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Toggle buttons must expose state programmatically.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Sample buttons carry aria-pressed, updated on every switch.

summary: Built and verified 2026-10-25 in the weekly hardening coverage sweep. Flagged Chromium 153 confirms the normalize contract live (raw vocabularies {M h q a Z}, {M H V h v Z}, {M C S Q T} all collapse to absolute M/L/C/Z; both panes render identically); unflagged shows the honest red unsupported verdict with both drawings still rendering from the raw string. Both-viewport screenshots read; console and network clean in all eight page runs.
